correlates.name: Zanamivir bronchospasm
correlates.presentation: 45-year-old man with COPD (FEV1 55% predicted) and 1 day of fever, myalgia and dry cough took his first dose of an inhaled dry-powder influenza antiviral. Within 30 minutes: chest tightness, RR 26, SpO2 88% on room air, prolonged expiration with diffuse wheezes
correlates.management: Stop the inhaled powder and give a short-acting bronchodilator; switch to oral oseltamivir. This inhaled antiviral is not recommended in asthma or COPD

correlates.name: Neuraminidase-inhibitor neuropsychiatric events
correlates.presentation: 11-year-old boy with rapid-antigen-positive influenza started a twice-daily oral antiviral suspension yesterday. Tonight he is confused and frightened, sees insects on the wall and tried to run outside. T 38.4 C, HR 110, neck supple, no focal deficits; it clears within hours
correlates.management: Stop the drug and observe him in a safe setting; these reactions are rare, transient and of unestablished cause, mostly in children and adolescents, and came to light in post-marketing surveillance

correlates.name: Amantadine neurotoxicity
correlates.presentation: 80-year-old man with Parkinson disease on hemodialysis for ESRD takes a renally cleared antiparkinsonian drug at his usual dose; diphenhydramine was added for sleep. Over 1 day he is suddenly not making sense, agitated and hallucinating. T 36.8 C, no focal deficits
correlates.management: Stop the drug and the antihistamine and support him while it clears slowly (half-life about 8 days in ESRD; dialysis does not remove it). Sudden onset in an older patient: think drug, not age
